- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates downside risk; add 5–15% buffer to low forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3.0), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated decline; cap subsequent drops at 1.5x prior peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — adjust for longer horizon (10+ days) by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — reduce forecast variance by 20–30% when sentiment >0.7.
